claims.statement: KNF's Recommendation S requires a comprehensive quantitative and qualitative affordability review and individualized treatment of irregular or unstable income rather than automatic exclusion.
Polish mortgage intermediaries are expressly defined as performing preparatory and administrative document work, so the proposed user and workflow are legally recognizable.

Hypothesis: pooled, consented outcome data can make lender routing for complex income materially better than broker spreadsheets, creating a defensible feedback loop if networks will contribute outcomes.

contrary_evidence: Large broker networks and banks already maintain internal policy matrices, calculators, and document portals.
Banks can change underwriting policy without public notice, making historical routing signals stale or misleading.

economics.acquisition_route: Pilot inside one broker network and one accounting channel, proving faster complete submission rather than promising higher approval
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 600 advisors at 12k PLN blended annual revenue produce 7.2M PLN revenue and about 2.5M PLN EBITDA by year 5. At 3.5x EBITDA and 65% ownership, equity is about 5.7M PLN in years 6 to 8, conditional on one network not controlling the data asset.
economics.founder_time: 12 to 18 hours weekly for product and model monitoring; a network partner owns consumer conversations
economics.gross_margin_basis: Expected 80% to 90% software gross margin after document processing; compliance, support, and policy verification are recurring costs
economics.payback: Saving two to four advisor hours or preventing one avoidable rework cycle per month can cover a seat; validate with time logs
economics.pricing: 799 PLN per advisor monthly plus 100 to 250 PLN per complex case, or 60,000 to 150,000 PLN annual network license
economics.retention_or_repeat: Advisors use it per complex application, and policy updates plus outcome benchmarks support annual contracts

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A versioned lender-policy and anonymized submission-outcome graph for irregular-income archetypes
fingerprint.customer: Licensed Polish mortgage-broker networks serving applicants with JDG and other irregular multi-source income
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Broker franchises, accounting platforms serving JDG clients, realtor networks, and mortgage training providers
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Document parser, transparent scenario engine, missing-evidence gate, and outcome-informed lender routing
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The broker network pays per advisor seat and per complex case prepared
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A broker receives a complex applicant file and must choose documentation, affordability scenarios, and a lender submission path

founder_fit: Combines the founder's finance interest, data-science ability, Polish context, and preference for measurable decision systems. Distribution can be concentrated through a few broker or accounting platforms, but compliance review and fairness testing are mandatory before processing real applications.
risks: A routing score may be interpreted as guaranteed approval or consumer financial advice.
Tax returns, statements, and household obligations are highly sensitive personal data.
Biased historical approvals can encode discriminatory lender behavior.

structure.control_point: The broker's lender-routing and file-completeness decision before submitting a complex mortgage case
structure.critical_dependency: Broker networks must contribute lawful, timely outcome data while keeping the product outside automated credit decision-making

thesis: Create a broker-side document and lender-fit engine for Polish mortgage applicants with sole-proprietor, dividend, foreign-currency, seasonal, or otherwise irregular income. It would parse tax returns, ZUS records, bank statements, and obligations; calculate transparent stability scenarios; flag missing evidence; and rank which lender policy deserves a human submission based on versioned broker-contributed outcomes. It does not approve credit or recommend debt to consumers; it helps licensed intermediaries prepare complex files.
title: JDG Mortgage Exception Engine for Polish Broker Networks
uncertainties: Number of complex-income applications per advisor and measurable time lost to avoidable lender submissions.
Whether broker networks may lawfully pool sufficiently detailed outcome features.
Whether a software vendor can remain outside regulated recommendation and credit-decision activity.
